title: Runway sensitivity scan — 1:1 prep
content:
Purpose and context:
- Quick prep for 1:1 with Alex (Head of Dedicated) — run a lightweight sensitivity scan and surface the minimal commit recommendations + risks.
- Focus: next 3-month runway, burst behavior, and fallback cost when reserved headroom is exhausted.
- Not final analysis: this is a talking draft to align on assumptions and get concrete decisions during the meeting.

Meeting details:
- When: 2026-03-12 10:30am PT (30m)
- Attendees: Alex, Maya (me), Ethan (ops), optional: Sofia (forecast)
- Deliverable: decision on whether to convert 100 GPU-hours/week of burst to reserve, and agreement on alert thresholds for autoscale fallback.

Assumptions (baseline):
- Base committed pool: 120 A100-equivalent GPUs (monthly reserve).
- Average utilization (prod gen workload): 62% steady, 85% peak 9–11am PT.
- Typical seq_len profile: 8k tokens avg for long-form customers (heavy tail), median 2k.
- Cost per GPU-hour (committed): $1.90 (effective after discounts). On-demand equivalent: $3.40/hr.
- Burst window tolerance: 30s p95 latency SLO, we allow 5% requests to hit fallback model variant.

Sensitivity scenarios (quick):
- Scenario A (Conservative): 10% higher median seq_len, burst factor +15%, no additional customers.
  - Expected additional GPU-hours/week: +420 GPU-hours
  - Impact: sustained utilization -> 72%, peak -> 92% (risk of queuing at 95th percentile).
  - Suggested action: convert 100 GPU-hours/week of burst allowance to reserved (trial 1 month).

- Scenario B (Optimistic growth): +2 new mid-size accounts onboard this quarter, usage adds +800 GPU-hours/week but with smoother profile (less bursty).
  - Expected utilization: +10–12% sustained, peak managed with autoscale.
  - Suggested action: keep burst policy; increase autoscale headroom to 200 GPU-hours but require stricter pre-warming for models with >4k seq_len.

- Scenario C (Burst storm): marketing spike + short experiments -> temporary +1500 GPU-hours/week (over 48 hours), but low median usage otherwise.
  - Impact: immediate exhaustion of burst pool, failover to on-demand causing cost spike (~$2.5k/day extra).
  - Suggested action: create emergency reserve buffer (on-call-approved) and automated alerting to flip to higher-priority queue + throttling rules.

Small quick table (week-level estimate):
- Week baseline consumption: 20,160 GPU-hours (120 GPUs * 24 * 7 * 0.62 utilization)
- Scenario A: +420 -> 20,580 GPU-hours
- Scenario B: +800 -> 20,960 GPU-hours
- Scenario C (during event window): spike add +1,500 over event week -> 21,660 GPU-hours

Runway math (3-month):
- Current reserved commit: 120 GPUs * 720 hours/month = 86,400 GPU-hours/month committed. (we bill monthly commit not per-week)
- Forecasted monthly demand baseline: ~87,360 GPU-hours (current utilization trends + small growth) -> ~1% overcommit risk.
- If Scenario B realized, monthly demand -> ~90,000 GPU-hours -> we need +2–4 GPUs committed on average to avoid frequent autoscale fallbacks.

Open questions to resolve in 1:1:
1) How tolerant is finance of temporary overrun vs signing a small addendum to the Dedicated contract this quarter? (Need Alex's signal)
2) If we convert 100 GPU-hours/week to reserved, who owns rollback? (SRE or Capacity ops?)
3) Can we tighten model pre-warm gating so long-sequence requests trigger a higher-priority warm path? (Tech ask to serving runtime team — see linked PR)
4) Do we want a hard budget cap that triggers automatic throttling + customer-facing notification? (Product decision)

Notes to self / things to say:
- Lead with the runway math and the low-cost step (convert 100 GPU-hours/week) as an experiment. Frame as reversible.
- Emphasize monitoring/alerts first: set alerts at 85% sustained util (24h) and at 92% peak (2h).
- Propose a short SLA for burst abuse detection and automated rate-limits (engineering can implement in 2 sprints).

Proposed agenda (10/20/30m split for a 30m slot):
- 0–5m: quick context and baseline numbers (I present)
- 5–15m: walk scenarios + trade-offs (open discussion)
- 15–25m: decisions requested (commit vs alerting threshold vs emergency buffer)
- 25–30m: agree next steps + owners

Post-meeting follow-ups (put into ticket backlog):
- Action 1: Draft short addendum proposal for +100 reserved GPU-hours/week trial (owner: Maya) — due 2026-03-19
- Action 2: Create SLO-based alerts in Datadog: sustained 85% (24h), peak 92% (2h) (owner: Ethan) — due 2026-03-16
- Action 3: Small serving change: pre-warm gating for >4k seq_len (owner: Sofia -> link ENG-4321) — due 2026-04-02
- Action 4: Write customer-facing throttling note template (owner: Product Ops) — assign after meeting, target 2026-03-26

Quick risks and mitigations:
- Risk: finance pushback on converting bursts to reserves -> Mitigation: run 30-day trial and cap spend delta, provide daily burn report.
- Risk: autoscale latency during cold starts for long seqs -> Mitigation: pre-warm + cache KV warming for heavy customers.
- Risk: mistaken assumptions on seq_len distribution -> Mitigation: run a 2-week stratified sample and revisit (add as a monitoring task).

Misc / scratch calculations (notes):
- If we commit an extra 5 GPUs (A100 equiv) 24/7: +5 * 720 = 3,600 GPU-hours/month. At $1.90/hr effective -> ~$6,840/month incremental.
- Equivalent on-demand cost for same hours: 3,600 * $3.40 = $12,240 -> commit saves ~$5,400/mo in that narrow case.

Links / references:
- Capacity model v2 (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Capacity+Runway+Model+v2
- Forecast ticket: JIRA-ENG-4321
- Serving PR for pre-warm gating: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve/pull/678

Final note: keep this lightweight. Main ask during 1:1 is the signal on finance tolerance (yes/no) and whether Alex is comfortable trialing a 100 GPU-hours/week conversion. If we get a yes, I will open the addendum draft + trigger alerts the same day.

-- end of draft --
